ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Preventive Visit — Franklin D. Roosevelt — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Periodic preventive visit; no new complaints. [S]

Mr. Roosevelt comes for his periodic preventive visit four weeks after his six-month heart failure review, at which the ejection fraction had improved to 45 percent. He completed the health risk assessment before the visit. The viral gastroenteritis in July settled within four days; he restarted all of his heart failure medicines on the third day without lightheadedness. He has had no emergency visits or hospital stays, no falls or transfer slips, and no skin breakdown. He has not smoked since April and finished the nicotine patch course in June; he reports occasional cravings during long meetings, which pass. He takes his medicines from a weekly organizer and has added no over-the-counter medicines or supplements. He has no new concerns. [S]

list.item:
Periodic preventive visit, age 62. Health risk assessment reviewed and a written prevention plan given. Depression and alcohol screens are negative. Because he has smoked more than 20 pack-years and quit less than 15 years ago, he qualifies for annual lung cancer screening. [S]
Next preventive visit in one year.

Heart failure with improved ejection fraction (I50.22). Ejection fraction 45 percent in September, up from 30 percent; KCCQ-12 78 and no congestion today. Guideline-directed therapy continues even though the ejection fraction has improved. [S]
Continue sacubitril/valsartan, carvedilol, spironolactone, empagliflozin, and atorvastatin without change.
Heart failure review with a basic metabolic panel in about three months, on the CMID schedule.

Hypertensive heart disease (I11.0). Blood pressure 120/74 mmHg, below the 130/80 target. [S]
No change.

Nicotine dependence, cigarettes, in early remission (F17.210). Abstinent for six months with brief cravings that pass. [S]
Relapse-prevention counseling given; restart a nicotine patch with a short-acting nicotine product at once if he smokes again.
Low-dose CT lung cancer screening after shared decision-making, below.

Prediabetes (R73.03). HbA1c 5.9 percent in March, with glucose values since then between 92 and 98 mg/dL. [S]
Repeat HbA1c with the heart failure laboratory tests in about three months.
Continue the low-sodium diet and seated exercise program.

Paraplegia after a paralytic illness at age 39; uses a manual wheelchair (B91). Skin intact and shoulders pain-free. Upper-limb overuse and pressure injury are the main long-term risks for a manual wheelchair user. [S]
Pressure relief every 15 to 30 minutes while seated and a daily skin check.
Use the transfer board and keep transfers level where possible to protect the shoulders.
Seating and wheelchair review by occupational therapy in one year, or sooner for shoulder pain.

Follow-up: Low-dose CT scan, stool test kit, and hepatitis C and HIV screening ordered. Zoster vaccine dose 2 in two to six months. Heart failure review with laboratory tests in about three months. Next preventive visit in one year. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 20 minutes, with his consent, prompted by his heart failure diagnosis. He has named a health care agent and agreed to complete a written health care directive naming that person; a blank form was given today. He wants full treatment, including hospital and intensive care, for any condition from which he could return to his work and present independence. He would not want prolonged life support if he could not communicate or recover. He will discuss these wishes with his agent and bring the completed form to his next visit. [S]
